newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent per lb weaker on Monday, as the July contract is set to expire after the close of business, dealers said.
Nearby support basis the benchmark October contract was pegged at 11.00 cents, followed by the recent low of 10.96 cents.
The July/October spread is expected to widen to a recent high, traders said. On Friday, October closed at a 0.22 cent premium to July.
The spot month closed 0.19 cent lower at 10.92 cents per lb on Friday. Most-active October settled 0.11 cent weaker at 11.14 cents, while the outer months settled 0.03 to 0.07 cent lower.

Then U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged planted area for sugarbeets and sugarcane for sugar and seed, at 1.4644 million acres in 1997, compared with 1.3684 million acres in 1996. Trading sources said the market has already absorbed the increase in planted area.
In London, white sugar futures were trading slightly lower in thin Monday trade. Volume was concentrated in the December and March contracts as players awaited the open of the New York market.
At 0847 EDT/1247 GMT, the spot August contract stood $0.50 lower at $320.80, while the rest of the board was trading $0.60 to $1.50 wealer.
